answer: A newcomer must finish a two-pole path under one custody key. It first completes a nadir drill: a unique rate-limited micro-task committed to a delayed-reveal hash. Midway it must sign a one-time raven challenge — a random ledger salt — in a short window, published before the hash opens. Only then can it take a zenith exam, a heavier sampled task. Votes attach only to completed paths. If two keys reuse a drill commitment or answer the same raven probe in correlated time, both paths are void and a reporter is paid from the deposit. Extra addresses add work, not votes.
